segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: And President Trump loves to talk about his TV ratings, if not his current approval

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: So he must be pleased to know that 33 million people watched the prime time rollout

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: of his Supreme Court pick, Neil Gorsuch.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: But what do Americans think of the choice?

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Well, a brand new CNN poll shows that a plurality, 39 percent, were left with a positive

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: first impression that compares with 45 percent for President Obama's never confirmed pick, Judge Merrick Garland,

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: and 54 percent, for now Chief Justice John Roberts.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: But when it comes to confirming the new nominee,

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: opinions are sharply divided along party lines.

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: Just 22% of Democrats think the Senate should vote to confirm him

segments.speaker: Unknown
segments.text: while an overwhelming 84% of Republicans do.
